methodological_rigor.justification: The study design is appropriate for its regulatory PK objective: an open-label, multi-cohort phase I/II trial with a pre-specified primary endpoint (AUC0-12 geometric mean 95% CI within 60-140% of SPRINT capsule exposure of 2,009 h×ng/mL), aligned with FDA guidance. Sample size was formally powered (≥10 per Global Cohort, 90% power, assumed intersubject gCV of 30%) and re-evaluated after enrollment, confirming 9 (GC1) and 11 (GC2) sufficed. Noncompartmental PK analysis in Phoenix WinNonlin and SAS v9.4 is standard; geometric means with 95% CI and MedDRA/CTCAE v5.0 coding are appropriate. Limitations include the small Japan Cohort (n=4, under-enrolled from 6), lack of a concurrent control arm (historical SPRINT comparator only), no efficacy data at DCO1, and single-dose PK estimates calculated over <3 half-lives (acknowledged by authors).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a prospective, single-arm, multi-cohort phase I/II PK/safety trial (non-randomized), classified as an individual cohort study on the Oxford CEBM scale (2b). Clinical relevance is high: the study directly supported FDA approval (September 10, 2025) of the selumetinib granule formulation for pediatric patients ≥1 year with symptomatic, inoperable NF1-PN, addressing a documented unmet need for young children unable to swallow capsules. Endpoints are regulatory-relevant (PK comparability enabling efficacy extrapolation from SPRINT) and the safety profile was characterized. Palatability was also assessed, with patient-centered endpoints bearing directly on adherence in a pediatric population.

reporting_quality.justification: CONSORT is the applicable framework for this interventional clinical trial (noting single-arm phase I/II design falls under CONSORT extensions). The manuscript reports ClinicalTrials.gov registration (NCT05309668), pre-specified primary and secondary endpoints, detailed eligibility, pre-specified AE definitions (CTCAE v5.0, MedDRA v26.1), dose-finding schema, and a formal sample-size justification referencing FDA guidance; participant flow (39 screened, 36 dosed) is reported. Minor gaps include limited within-manuscript detail on allocation to cohorts and reliance on an external Data Supplement for many methods. Data/code availability is weak: no mention of raw data deposition, individual-level data access, or analytical code; this is typical for industry-sponsored trials but limits reproducibility.

novelty_literature.justification: Novelty is primarily formulation and population: the study provides the first pediatric PK/safety data for the selumetinib granule formulation in children ≥1 to <7 years, extending access to younger patients who cannot swallow capsules. Conceptually incremental—MEK1/2 inhibition in NF1-PN was established by SPRINT and the capsule formulation was already approved; the granule formulation's relative bioavailability in healthy adults was previously reported (Cohen-Rabbie et al., 2022, ref 22). The main contribution is bridging PK exposure across age/BSA strata to enable regulatory extrapolation—a meaningful empirical and translational extension but not a mechanistic or paradigm-shifting advance.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-organized with a clear IMRaD structure; the abstract is quantitatively grounded (geometric mean AUC0-12 values with 95% CIs, cohort sizes, AE frequencies) and accurately reflects the body. Terminology is precise, acronyms are defined on first use (e.g., AUC0-12, GC1/GC2/JC, BSA, AESI), and the discussion appropriately addresses limitations (short DCO1 duration, PK estimates over <3 half-lives, small JC). Figure and table captions are informative and self-contained. Minor repetition occurs between results and discussion regarding the 60-140% PK acceptance criterion.

key_strengths: Pre-specified primary PK endpoint with 60-140% acceptance range per FDA guidance, formally powered (90%) and met in both Global Cohorts
Direct regulatory relevance: findings supported FDA approval (Sep 2025) of the granule formulation for children ≥1 year with NF1-PN
Manageable safety profile characterized over median ~11 months exposure, consistent with the established capsule profile
Patient-centered palatability assessment showing improvement from C1 to C7, addressing a real adherence barrier in young children
Clear reporting of sample-size justification, re-evaluation after enrollment, and transparent limitations
key_concerns: Small single-arm design with historical SPRINT comparator rather than concurrent control; under-enrolled Japan Cohort (n=4 of planned 6)
No efficacy data at DCO1; conclusions on clinical benefit rely on PK-based extrapolation from SPRINT
Single-dose PK estimates calculated over <3 half-lives, limiting precision of some parameters (acknowledged)
Data and analytical code availability not addressed; reproducibility posture weak
Incremental novelty—new formulation of an already-approved drug with mechanism and efficacy previously established
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically solid, pivotal pediatric PK/safety study with direct regulatory impact but incremental scientific novelty and limited sample size/follow-up; plausibly accepted at a Tier 2 oncology venue with minor revisions, falling short of Tier 1 given the lack of efficacy endpoints and purely bridging nature of the contribution.
